name: Pueblo of Zia grant, confirmed by Congress December 22, 1858 (Royce Area 675)
aka: Pueblo de Zia v. United States, ICC Docket 137
citation: Act of Congress confirming the Pueblo grants, 11 Stat. 374 (confirmed December 22, 1858; patented 1864), as listed by Royce; not a treaty
promises: Not a treaty. Royce lists the Sia (Zia) Pueblo grant as a Spanish grant of 1689, confirmed by the United States on December 22, 1858 (11 Stat. 374) and patented in 1864, of 17,514.63 acres. This was land the Pueblo kept.
The date 1886-10-01 is the heading under which Royce printed the Pueblo grants, not the date of any act concerning Zia.
Outside the grant, the Court of Claims held in 1964 that Zia, Jemez and Santa Ana together held Indian title in 1848 to 298,634 acres of the tract they claimed.
landTaken: None documented inside the grant. (Docket 137: 282,415.73 acres of aboriginal land outside the grants, held jointly with Jemez and Santa Ana.)
compensation: None for this grant documented. Outside the grant, Docket 137 ended in a joint settlement of $749,083.75 for Zia, Jemez and Santa Ana (January 10, 1974), after a vacated 1971 award of $766,936.08.
today: Outside the grant: in Indian Claims Commission Docket 137 (Zia, Jemez and Santa Ana jointly), the Court of Claims held in 1964 that the three Pueblos had aboriginal title to 298,634 acres of public domain around their grants (165 Ct. Cl. 501), and the Commission found on December 17, 1970 that the United States took 282,415.73 acres of it, worth $938,000, without compensation; the claim ended in a $749,083.75 settlement on January 10, 1974. The Spanish grants were expressly outside that claim, so it is not counted against this grant. The 1974 judgment closed Docket 137 for Zia, Jemez and Santa Ana together. The Commission first dismissed the claim in 1962; the Court of Claims reversed in 1964.

openQuestions: The Royce row is the confirmed grant, land Zia kept. The breach recorded is the taking of the shared aboriginal land outside it found in Docket 137, which also covers Jemez (cession-1886-10-01-jemez-pueblo, marked sameEventAs this record) and Santa Ana.
The Pueblo of Zia's own account was not found: its website did not load and no tribal history page came up in searches.
Pueblo Lands Board findings on non-Indian claims inside the Zia grant were not searched in this pass.
How the 1974 judgment was divided among the three Pueblos was not traced.
treaties.json date 1886-10-01 is Royce's column heading, not an event date for Zia (noted, not edited).

Audit 2026-11-08 (round 14): status lowered from broken to no-breach-found. The breaches all concerned Docket 137, aboriginal land outside the Spanish grants; the Court of Claims (165 Ct. Cl. 501) records that the Pueblos conceded no claim to the patented grants. This record maps Royce's grant (land kept), so the finding is not about this row and was moved to today. Pueblo Lands Board findings inside the Zia grant remain a lead; Zia is not named in the 1933 Act.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Pueblo, Zia, Zia grant; United States v. Pueblo de Zia, 200 Ct. Cl. 601 (1973) is the Docket 137 aboriginal claim, already recorded; the ICC aboriginal-title decisions found expressly exclude the confirmed grants (e.g. 30 Ind. Cl. Comm. 234, 1973), so nothing new inside this grant.
